propositions: Dense multi-criterion completion runs exhaust bounded request budgets with zero CriterionBank writes when Pydantic AI executes concurrent tool batches, violating the incremental banking contract.
Prompt-only instructions cannot enforce one repository action per model response; concurrent tool execution defers all record calls until budget exhaustion leaves zero banked criterion verdicts.

An explicit completion-only policy wrapper at the agent toolset seam must atomically claim one governed action per run_step, count evidence responses per criterion, and invoke fallback met=false recording on the third response if still unbanked.

The policy attaches frozen CompletionEvidencePolicy metadata to record tools in both primary and successor completion paths, reusing existing record_criterion_verdict semantics with a three-response cap and live per-criterion boundary reset.

The simple three-criterion control and proof that authority placement (system prompt finite loop vs untrusted ticket context) determines banking success demonstrates the root cause and validates the remedy design.

Original reproduction (0 banks after 24 requests) transitions to GREEN bounded success (>=2/3 trials with normal verdict) under the merged policy; disabling the policy returns defect-seeded mutation to RED (0/3 bounded success).
